To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current practices and particular challenges in disaster relief SCM are different from those in commercial SCM and that corporations can help disaster relief agencies overcome these differences through cross-sector collaborations.
the development of disaster relief supply chain practices requires the development of cross-sector socially oriented collaborations.

(1) the dual-cycle model provides a concise and comprehensive representation of current practices of SCM and logistics management in the context of disaster relief; (2) the dual-cycle framework identifies challenges and barriers to more efficient SCM practices in disaster relief operations and (3) the dual-cycle conceptualization offers a simple, functional representation of how cross-sector collaborations between corporations and humanitarian organizations might help disaster relief agencies meet SCM and logistics challenges.
